decisions.reason: Organic sliced ham fits a growing organic segment and an existing packaging line, so it costs little to keep while its demand is still being proven.
Organic Kasseler extends the same low-cost organic range, and its niche demand is still uncertain enough to justify keeping the option open.
Organic pepper salami is a mainstream flavour in a growing organic line, so keeping it costs little and its upside remains plausible.
An exotic teriyaki aspic for service counters is a narrow niche with no signs of traction since launch, so its value is unlikely to be realized and the resources are better used elsewhere.
Fennel salami got a page of its own, which signals firm commitment, and specialty salami fits the core range at low marginal cost.
A classic veal liver pâté is close to the firm's established products and cheap to maintain, so there is no strong signal to abandon it.
